text:
Ava: eu-west-1 reporting degraded GPU capacity, autoscaler drained some nodes. Starting DNS-based traffic shift to eu-central as a precaution.
Sam (netops): doing weighted DNS shift via provider API, lowering eu-west weight to 10% and raising eu-central to 90%. TTL still 300s from last config though.
Priya (sre): heads up — a lot of public resolvers are still serving the old records because TTL was 300. We should drop TTL before aggressive shifts next time.
Luca (infra): too late to retroactively force every resolver; changing TTL now only helps for new queries. But we can do a staged weight shift over 15m to reduce cache churn.
Sam (netops): agreed. I'll push a small weight change every 3m: 75 -> 60 -> 40 -> 20 -> 10. Will also set record TTL to 30s now via API.
Sam (netops): API call I ran:
```
curl -X PATCH "https://api.dnsprovider.example/v1/zones/ZONE/records/example.redwood.cloud" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DNS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"ttl":30, "records": [{"type":"A","values":["34.201.12.45","34.201.12.46"]}]}'
```
Priya (sre): saw mixed dig output from global probes, some resolvers still returning eu-west IPs. Example:
```
$ dig +short example.redwood.cloud @8.8.8.8
34.201.12.45
```
and from another resolver:
```
$ dig +short example.redwood.cloud @1.1.1.1
3.120.66.10
```
Ava: that matches users reporting intermittent routing to degraded cluster. Any sign of resolver-level rate limiting or EDNS weirdness?
Sam (netops): maybe. Noticed some large ISPs returning stale answers for up to 10m beyond TTL change, probably due to resolver cache priming and upstream caching layers. Also saw some resolvers ignore our low-TTL update because we changed records and TTL in the same API transaction — some providers re-serve the previous RRset until propagation completes.
Priya (sre): fallback plan: enable application-level graceful degradation on affected nodes and expand cross-region fallback in servicemesh. We can also temporarily increase capacity in eu-central (spin burst GPUs) but that costs money. Thoughts?
Luca (infra): spinning burst nodes now (estimate +40% cost for 2h). Doing canary deploy of fallback routing in 5m.
Ava: do it. Prioritize reliability. Track cost and tag resources for chargeback.
Sam (netops): quick checklist I'm following:
- set TTL=30 (done)
- staged weight updates every 3m (in progress)
- check authoritative NS consistency across providers (in progress)
- contact DNS vendor support if authoritative answers diverge (>5m)
- coordinate with CDN/caching teams to purge / prefetch as needed

Sam (netops): checking NS consistency:
```
$ dig NS example.redwood.cloud +short @ns1.dnsprovider.example
ns1.dnsprovider.example.
ns2.dnsprovider.example.
```
No divergence so far, authoritative zone looks OK.
Priya (sre): opened an incident channel and flagged the APAC customer ops queue about possible 15-30m inconsistent routing. Adding runbook note: avoid TTL changes and weight shifts in same second when possible; always pre-warm lower TTL at low-traffic window.
Ava: also add a note about EDNS0/response-size issues — some corporate resolvers truncate and fallback to TCP which slows things and can cause timeouts.
Sam (netops): good call. Will include a small diagnostic command for support to run: `dig @<resolver> example.redwood.cloud +edns=0 +bufsize=4096` to check behavior.
Luca (infra): rolling out mesh-level sticky session fallback so users on stale resolvers see a degraded but consistent experience rather than half-success half-failure.
Priya (sre): monitoring: watch 5xx rate on eu-west and latency tail on eu-central; also watch DNS RCODE from probes.
Ava: timeline: 1749998888 - incident opened, 1749998950 - TTL lowered to 30, 1749999000 - staged weights started, 1749999040 - cross-region burst capacity live.
deploy-bot: deployment eu-central/fallback enabled (canary) :rocket:
Sam (netops): vendor engineering confirmed a short window where their edge caches re-seeded stale records; they cleared caches on request. Expect full convergence in ~10m.
Priya (sre): ok seeing drop in errors from a subset of probes, but still noisy in APAC. Continue staggered shift, no sudden swaps.
Ava: post-incident actions (short):
- formalize TTL pre-stage playbook (set TTL to 30 during non-incident prep windows)
- add resolver-consistency probe to our synthetic suite (global)
- doc vendor caveats about simultaneous RRset+TTL updates
- cost review for burst GPU policy and tagging automation
Luca (infra): i'll create a ticket for auto-burst tagging + budget guardrails.
Sam (netops): i'll add a DNS vendor runbook section with exact API commands and recommended delays.
Priya (sre): closing this thread when 95th pct errors back to baseline and DNS probes show consistent answers for 10m.
Ava: great work. Keep chime updates lean. :thumbsup:
